# A morning

In 1446, a book introduced Hangeul (한글), the Korean alphabet. It opened by
stating the entire system in a few pages: every letter, and the rules for
combining letters. The explanations came only after those pages. The book's
postface made a claim about speed: *a wise man can learn the letters before the
morning is over.*

This part makes the same claim. It is short on purpose, so that you can finish
it in a single reading. It holds a first plot, then gog's whole vocabulary in
one table, then practice. The practice has two halves: first reading finished
sentences, then writing your own. The second half also shows the refusals you
are most likely to see.

This part covers each idea only briefly. Nearly every idea you meet here has a
full chapter later in the book. The morning teaches three skills instead. When
it is over, you should be able to read any gog sentence, in this book or in a
colleague's script. You should also be able to write a sentence that answers
your own question, and to predict whether gog will draw that sentence or
refuse it.
